review_output: {"summary":"Scoped pure-helper review. The window, [S,T) and T-1 boundary, inclusive 7-day maturity, dedupe and fail-closed paths look consistent, and the supplied tests trace correctly. Two first-crossing/rounding issues remain. (1) Crossing is recomputed on inward-rounded clipped segments, so it can differ from the durable unclipped crossing and wrongly invalidate the report. (2) The floored-media comparator disagrees with the documented exact-rational ceiling, and one test pins the disagreement. Three lower-severity items follow. No other regressions found.","findings":[{"severity":"MAJOR","confidence":0.55,"area":"first-crossing consistency / reconciliation","file":"src/lib/live-core-metrics-read-model.ts","issue":"Completion is derived from segments already clipped by clipPlaybackSegment, which rounds media coordinates inward (ceil start, floor end). The clipped segment has a different slope than the original, and partialMediaMs then floors against that new slope.","evidence":"viewingMetrics: clipPlaybackSegment(row, max(verifiedAt,S), T-1) -> firstCompletionTime(clipped). The durable completion is presumably computed from the unclipped segment. orderMetrics requires firstCompletion === derivedAt.","impact":"A crossing before T can shift by about 1 ms (or more at low rates) when a segment straddles verification or T-1. A correct durable fact then becomes invalid_data and takes the whole order metric down.","recommended_fix":"Do not re-slope clipped rows. Evaluate crossing on the original segments with a lower media-eligibility bound (verification) and an upper wall cutoff T-1. Alternatively keep the original slope when clipping. Document that durable completion uses the same post-verification clip.","required_test":"A non-integer-rate segment (e.g. 29970/30000) clipped at verification and at T-1, where the unclipped crossing is before T-1. Assert derived crossing equals the unclipped crossing."},{"severity":"MAJOR","confidence":0.55,"area":"rounding convention","file":"src/lib/live-viewing-evidence.ts","issue":"The comments say crossing is the exact rational crossing rounded up to an integer ms. The code floors media coverage at each integer wall ms before testing the 90% threshold, so it can report a later ms than the ceiling of the exact crossing.","evidence":"firstCompletionTime(3,[wall 0-10, media 0-3]): exact 2.7 media is reached at t=9 (0.3*9), but partialMediaMs gives floor(2.7)=2, so the result is 10. The test titled 'integer ceiling' pins 10.","impact":"Crossing and order eligibility can be late by 1-4 ms, changing T-boundary inclusion and maturity. This contradicts the stated convention and the prior MAJOR2 intent.","recommended_fix":"Either compare exact rational coverage (scaled integers) and take ceil, or explicitly redefine coverage as whole floored media milliseconds, and fix docs and tests and the ingestion contract accordingly.","required_test":"Table test comparing the implementation to an exact BigInt rational oracle for multiple rates and durations, including d=3, wall 10, media 3 (expect 9 under the exact convention)."},{"severity":"MINOR","confidence":0.5,"area":"availability / fail closed","file":"src/lib/live-core-metrics-read-model.ts","issue":"A single person exceeding MAX_COMPLETION_SEGMENTS (limit_exceeded) is converted by requireFact into invalid_data for every metric, including attendance and average viewing, which do not depend on completion.","evidence":"requireFact(completion.status === 'available') inside the per-person loop; the catch returns invalid for all five metrics.","impact":"One long or noisy history, whether legitimate or hostile, wipes out the whole report. The 10,000 cap is about 2.8 h at 1 s heartbeats.","recommended_fix":"Separate limit_exceeded from invalid facts: keep wall-based metrics and mark completion/order unavailable with a distinct reason. Alternatively compact adjacent segments before the cap.","required_test":"One person with 10,001 segments and others normal: attendance and average remain available, completion and order are unavailable with a limit reason."},{"severity":"MINOR","confidence":0.4,"area":"order state integrity","file":"src/lib/live-core-metrics-read-model.ts","issue":"OrderFact has no order identity or state version. Stale non-cancelled snapshots of an order that was later cancelled cannot be detected, and any one qualifying row for a person qualifies them.","evidence":"orderMetrics validates only personId, time and boolean; qualification adds the person if any row qualifies.","impact":"A retransmitted or stale pre-cancellation row can overstate conversions. This is only safe if the adapter guarantees one current row per order.","recommended_fix":"Add orderId (and ideally a version) to the contract. Reject conflicting states per order, or state in the type that rows must be current, deduplicated snapshots.","required_test":"Same orderId given as cancelled=false then cancelled=true: expect invalid_data or exclusion, not qualification."},{"severity":"NIT","confidence":0.4,"area":"exported helper robustness","file":"src/lib/live-viewing-evidence.ts","issue":"The exported clipPlaybackSegment accepts unvalidated numbers. BigInt() throws RangeError on NaN or fractional values, and a negative delta truncates toward zero instead of rounding inward. Internally the read model validates first, but other callers may not.","evidence":"BigInt(row.wallEndMs - row.wallStartMs) and BigInt(start - row.wallStartMs) with no validSegment or integer check.","impact":"Misuse throws a non-domain exception or produces an inconsistent clip.","recommended_fix":"Validate integer inputs and a monotone row and return null, or make the function module-private.","required_test":"clipPlaybackSegment with NaN, a fractional start, and mediaEnd<mediaStart returns null without throwing."}]}
